test_title: PYST 22: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 14 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A 250 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 7 km/hr (in same direction) in 50 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will this train take to completely cross another 280 m long train, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 28 km/hr?
solution:
**Given:**

Length of train = 250 m

Speed of man = 7 km/hr

Overtaking time = 50 sec

Length of second train = 280 m

Speed of second train = 28 km/hr (opposite direction)

**Formula used:**

Relative speed = Difference (same direction), Sum (opposite direction)

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed (in m/s) = km/hr × 5/18

**Calculation:**

Let speed of train = x km/hr

Relative speed with man = (x - 7) km/hr

⇒ (x - 7) × 5/18 = 250 / 50

⇒ (x - 7) × 5/18 = 5

⇒ x - 7 = 18

⇒ x = 25 km/hr

Speed of train = 25 km/hr

Now, relative speed with second train (opposite direction) = (25 + 28) = 53 km/hr

⇒ 53 × 5/18 = 265/18 m/s

Total length to cross = 250 + 280 = 530 m

Time = 530 ÷ (265/18)

⇒ Time = 530 × 18 / 265

⇒ Time = 36 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is Option (1).**
